verdict.rationale: The evidence shows no user-defined rules engine that triggers actions automatically on events. Webhooks only notify an external endpoint when jobs complete or fail. That is a developer building block a consumer could use to build automation, not first-party event-to-action rules. Classify's 'natural-language rules' categorize documents rather than trigger actions, and the n8n node is an external host-platform workaround.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: you can configure webhook endpoints to be notified immediately when jobs complete, fail, or reach other states
